MATTHEW.|81 HOLY weeke.}}</noinclude>vvould. {{verse|chapter=27|verse=16}} And he had then a notorious pri{{ls}}oner, that vvas called Barabbas. {{verse|chapter=27|verse=17}} They therfore being gathered together, Pilate {{ls}}aid: whom vvil you that I relea{{ls}}e to you, Barabbas, or {{sc|Iesvs}} that is called Chri{{ls}}t? {{verse|chapter=27|verse=18}} For he knevve that for enuie they had deliuered him. {{verse|chapter=27|verse=19}} And as he vvas {{ls}}itting in place of iudgment, his vvife {{ls}}ent vnto him, {{ls}}aying: Haue thou nothing to doe vvith that iu{{ls}}t man. for I haue {{ls}}uffred many things this day in my {{ls}}leepe for him. {{verse|chapter=27|verse=20}} But the cheefe Prie{{ls}}tes and auncients per{{ls}}uaded the people, that they {{ls}}hould a{{ls}}ke Barabbas, and make {{sc|Iesvs}} avvay. {{verse|chapter=27|verse=21}} And the Pre{{ls}}ident an{{ls}}vvering, {{ls}}aid to them: Whether vvil you of the tvvo to be relea{{ls}}ed vnto you? But they {{ls}}aid, Barabbas. {{verse|chapter=27|verse=22}} Pilate {{ls}}aith to them, what {{ls}}hal I doe then vvith {{sc|Iesvs}} that is called Chri{{ls}}t? They {{ls}}ay al, Let him be crucified. {{verse|chapter=27|verse=23}} The Pre{{ls}}ident {{ls}}aid to them, why vvhat euil hath he done? But they cried the more, {{ls}}aying, Let him be crucified. {{verse|chapter=27|verse=24}} And Pilate {{ls}}eeing that he nothing preuailed, but rather tumult vvas tovvard: taking vvater he vva{{ls}}hed his hands before the people, {{ls}}aying, I am {{sup|‖}} innocent of the bloud of this iu{{ls}}t man: looke you to it. {{verse|chapter=27|verse=25}} And the vvhole people an{{ls}}vvering, {{ls}}aid, His bloud be vpon vs, and vpon our children. {{verse|chapter=27|verse=26}} Then he relea{{ls}}ed to them Barabbas, and hauing {{ls}}courged {{sc|Iesvs}}, deliuered him vnto them for to be crucified.

{{verse|chapter=27|verse=27}} Then the Pre{{ls}}idents {{ls}}ouldiars taking {{sc|Iesvs}} into the Palace, gathered together vnto him the vvhole band: {{verse|chapter=27|verse=28}} {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Io. 19, 2.''}}* and {{ls}}tripping him, put a {{ls}}carlet cloke about him, {{verse|chapter=27|verse=29}} and platting a crovvne of thornes, put it vpon his head, and a reede in his right hand. And bovving the knee before him, they mocked him, {{ls}}aying, Haile King of the Iewes. {{verse|chapter=27|verse=30}} And {{ls}}pitting vpon him, they tooke the reede, and {{ls}}mote his head. {{verse|chapter=27|verse=31}} And after they had mocked him, they tooke of the cloke from him, and put on him his ovvne garments, and led him avvay to crucifie him. {{verse|chapter=27|verse=32}} And in going they found a man of Cyréne, named Simon: him they forced to take vp his cro{{ls}}{{ls}}e. {{verse|chapter=27|verse=33}} {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text={{sc|Hora {{ls}}exta}} in the Churches Seruice.}}And they came into the place that is called Golgotha, vvhich is, the place of Caluarie. {{verse|chapter=27|verse=34}} And they gaue him vvine to drinke mingled vvith gall. And vvhen he had ta{{ls}}ted, he vvould not drinke.

{{verse|chapter=27|verse=35}} And after they had crucified him, they deuided his garments, ca{{ls}}ting lottes: that it might be fulfilled vvhich vvas {{ls}}poken by the Prophet, {{ls}}aying: {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''P{{ls}}. 21, 19.''}}''They deuided my garments among''<noinclude>{{rh||L|them:}}</noinclude>
